(1) The pool: 'The U.S. adult pneumococcal market generated estimated annual sales of more than $1.5 billion in 2025' (Vaxcyte FY2025 10-K, 0001649094-26-000007; the FY2024 10-K, 0001649094-25-000028, put 2024 at 'approximately $1 billion to $2 billion'). (2) The share: Capvaxive (Merck's PCV21), the last broader-coverage conjugate to enter that market, sold $730mm in the United States in 2025, its first full year (Merck FY2025 10-K 0000310158-26-000063, product axis), 48.7% of $1,500mm. VAX-31 at that share of that pool is $730mm a year in the US
column12: US adults only, held flat at the 2025 pool: Pfizer reports 'lower vaccination rates in the pediatric and adult indications in the U.S., as well as market share erosion for the adult indication in the U.S.' with Prevnar US sales of $1,801mm in the first half of 2026 against $2,030mm (10-Q 0000078003-26-000095; six-month table in 8-K exhibit 0000078003-26-000094), so no growth is evidenced. Case for higher: the pool is a floor ('more than'); VAX-31 is designed to cover about 95% of IPD in US adults 50 and older, with 'the potential to provide incremental coverage of 13-36% of invasive pneumococcal disease' over the available adult conjugates, and met noninferiority to both in OPUS-1 (8-K exhibit 99.1, 0001193125-26-413168), and Prevnar 20 took 96.6% of the Medicare Part B adult conjugate class within three years of its ACIP recommendation (CMS Part B spending by drug, 2022 to 2024); Capvaxive itself grew 38% worldwide in the first half of 2026, $326mm against $236mm (Merck quarterly filings, as asset_revenue holds them); OPUS-3 could open revaccination of adults who had a lower-valency vaccine. Case for lower: a third entrant splits the market three ways where Capvaxive split it two; Capvaxive 'did not receive a preferred recommendation despite its disease coverage' (Vaxcyte FY2025 10-K) and none is assured for VAX-31; serotypes 3 and 12F missed the 0.667 noninferiority margin against PCV21; Pfizer's 25-valent conjugate began a registrational pediatric Phase 3 in May 2026 and a 35-valent adult candidate is expected to enter the clinic (8-K exhibit 0000078003-26-000094). Not modelled: sales outside the US, the infant indication (Phase 2) and the Sutro regulatory milestones of up to $60.0mm

column11: filed plan: OPUS-2 and OPUS-3 report in the first half of 2027, 'Supporting Planned Biologics License Application Submission in First Half of 2028' (8-K exhibit 99.1, 0001193125-26-413168), after a manufacturing consistency study, the final Phase 3 study before the BLA (10-Q 0001649094-26-000043). A priority review acts about eight months after submission and a standard one about twelve, so a decision falls between about September 2028 and mid-2029, and the last adult conjugate was recommended within days of approval (Capvaxive, approved June 2024, https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/merck-pneumococcal-vaccine-fda-approval-capvaxive/719227/; ACIP vote 27 June 2024, https://www.merck.com/news/cdcs-acip-unanimously-recommends-mercks-capvaxive-pneumococcal-21-valent-conjugate-vaccine-for-pneumococcal-vaccination-in-appropriate-adults/). column11: derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Solved so the modelled book reproduces that margin rather than assumed from one line's cost structure: the alliance rows carry no cost of sales and Animal Health carries its own, so a ratio taken off a single product does not reconcile the company. The window barely matters here, unlike Pfizer: the same aggregate is 21.9% over five years and 21.3% over every year on file. Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 7.48% to 2.06%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 2.06% to -1.23%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3610 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3746 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -1.3576%.
